newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Three feared dead after heavy Venezuela rains.
newsitem.headline: Three feared dead after heavy Venezuela rains.

text.p: Two children and a man were feared dead, swept away by a raging river after three days of downpours in the central Venezuela, authorities said on Friday.
Houses were washed away and a bridge collapsed in the rising waters and mudslides that have left more than 150 families homeless, Manuel Lopez of the Miranda State Emergency Institute told Reuters.
"The entire Valles del Tuy area has collapsed," said Lopez in reference to the densely-populated valley about 40 miles (60 km) southeast of Caracas.
Local residents said two children and a man had drowned after falling into the raging river Tuy Lopez said, but this could not be officially confirmed.
Houses in the shanty towns that cling precariously to the valley sides surrounding the capital are frequently washed away during the summer wet season.
The heavy rains came as rescuers in eastern Venezuela continued to search for survivors of a powerful earthquake that killed at least 68 people, many of them children buried in their classrooms.
